title: Germany: 6% surcharge for all customers, no phasing
statement: Apply a 6% freight surcharge to all German customers, including contract customers, from 1 March 2023, with no phasing.
rationale: Fuel and linehaul costs were rising and the country manager wanted one clean move rather than a staged one.
expected_outcome: About +$4.8M a quarter with churn loss near 0.8% of baseline revenue.

evidence.excerpt: Apply a 6% freight surcharge to all German customers, including contract customers, effective 1 March 2023, with no phasing.

title: Germany: roll back to 2% and exempt contract customers
statement: Roll the German surcharge back to 2% and exempt high-volume contract customers until their next renewal.
rationale: The 6% surcharge triggered a competitive response and contract customer disputes; revenue fell instead of rising.
alternatives: Keep 6% and negotiate account by account
expected_outcome: +$1.2M a quarter with churn loss near 0.5% of baseline.

evidence.excerpt: Roll the German surcharge back to 2% and exempt high-volume contract customers until their next renewal.
Eleven high-volume contract customers have disputed the 6% surcharge, citing fixed-price clauses.

title: Benelux: 3% surcharge as an eight-week pilot
statement: Run a 3% freight surcharge pilot in Benelux for eight weeks, exempting high-volume contract customers, with weekly revenue and churn checks.
rationale: After Germany, the team chose to test in a smaller market before scaling.
expected_outcome: +$1.5M a quarter with churn loss at 0.6% of baseline.

evidence.excerpt: Run a 3% freight surcharge pilot in Benelux for eight weeks, exempting high-volume contract customers, with weekly revenue and churn checks.

title: France: 5% surcharge with contract exemption and 60-day review
statement: Apply a 5% freight surcharge in France from 1 February 2024, exempting high-volume contract customers, with an executive review after 60 days.
rationale: Service scores in France were strong, and the Pricing Director agreed on condition that contract customers stayed out and a 60-day review was held.
expected_outcome: +$3.2M a quarter with churn loss of 1.0% of baseline.

evidence.excerpt: Apply a 5% freight surcharge in France from 1 February 2024, exempting high-volume contract customers, with an executive review after 60 days.

title: Nordics: 4% surcharge in two phases
statement: Introduce a 4% freight surcharge in the Nordics in two phases: Sweden and Denmark first, then Norway and Finland after a four-week check.
rationale: Phasing by country allowed a check after four weeks before the second pair of markets.
expected_outcome: +$2.0M a quarter with churn loss of 0.8% of baseline.

evidence.excerpt: Approved at the Nordics pricing board: introduce a 4% freight surcharge in two phases, Sweden and Denmark first, then Norway and Finland after a four-week check.

title: Iberia: 7% surcharge without a pilot
statement: Apply a 7% freight surcharge across Iberia from 1 June 2024 without a pilot phase.
rationale: Iberia margins were the weakest in Europe and the country manager wanted a bigger step than France took.
alternatives: A smaller step, given the price-sensitive SME base
expected_outcome: +$2.6M a quarter with churn loss of 1.2% of baseline.

evidence.excerpt: Apply a 7% freight surcharge across Iberia from 1 June 2024 without a pilot phase.

title: Italy: 5% surcharge before billing was ready
statement: Apply a 5% freight surcharge in Italy on 10 June 2024, before the billing rate tables were updated and tested.
expected_outcome: +$2.4M a quarter with churn loss of 1.0% of baseline.

evidence.excerpt: The Italy country team applied a 5% freight surcharge on 10 June 2024 before the billing rate tables were updated and tested.

title: Poland and CEE: hold the surcharge at 0% to win volume
statement: Hold the freight surcharge at 0% in Poland and CEE for two quarters and prioritise volume growth.
rationale: Two competitors had raised surcharges in Poland; holding price was expected to win their volume.
alternatives: Follow the France approach and raise the surcharge
expected_outcome: No surcharge revenue; volume growth at thinner margin.

evidence.excerpt: Hold the freight surcharge at 0% in Poland and CEE for two quarters and prioritise volume growth.

title: UK and Ireland: 5% surcharge with two weeks' notice
statement: Announce a 5% freight surcharge in the UK and Ireland on 11 November 2024 with two weeks' notice to all customers.
expected_outcome: +$2.8M a quarter with churn loss of 1.0% of baseline.

evidence.excerpt: The UK and Ireland team announced a 5% freight surcharge on 11 November 2024 with two weeks' notice to all customers.

title: Europe: adopt a 1.2% churn guardrail for all surcharges
statement: Adopt a churn guardrail for all European surcharges: pause and review if churn-related revenue loss exceeds 1.2% of baseline revenue.
rationale: Germany 2023 and Iberia 2024 both exceeded planned churn loss by a wide margin before anyone paused.
expected_outcome: Surcharges above 3% start as phased pilots with weekly KPI checks and a 60-day executive review.

evidence.excerpt: Adopt a churn guardrail for all European surcharges: pause and review if churn-related revenue loss exceeds 1.2% of baseline revenue.
Every surcharge above 3% starts as a phased pilot with weekly KPI checks and a 60-day executive review.

title: Germany: raise to 3% with contract customers exempt
statement: Raise the German freight surcharge to 3% from 1 May 2025, keep high-volume contract customers exempt, and monitor competitor rates weekly.
rationale: Trust had been rebuilt since 2023 and the country manager supported a modest step if contract accounts stayed protected.
expected_outcome: +$2.2M a quarter with churn loss of 0.6% of baseline.

evidence.excerpt: Raise the German freight surcharge to 3% from 1 May 2025, keep high-volume contract customers exempt, and monitor competitor rates weekly.

title: Europe: exclude contract customers from mid-term surcharges
statement: Exclude high-volume contract customers from any mid-term freight surcharge in Europe; apply changes only at contract renewal.
rationale: Every surcharge dispute traced back to charging contract customers mid-term.
expected_outcome: Roughly a tenth of the eligible revenue base is out of scope, in exchange for removing the dispute risk.

evidence.excerpt: Exclude high-volume contract customers from any mid-term freight surcharge in Europe; apply changes only at contract renewal.
Excluding them takes roughly a tenth of the eligible revenue base out of scope, but it removes the dispute risk.

title: US Midwest: 8% fuel-linked surcharge
statement: Introduce an 8% fuel-linked surcharge in the US Midwest, indexed to a published diesel benchmark.
rationale: Index-linked surcharges are standard practice in that market and competitors moved at the same time.
expected_outcome: +$5.0M a quarter with churn loss of 1.0% of baseline.

evidence.excerpt: In April 2024 the US Midwest business introduced an 8% fuel-linked surcharge indexed to a published diesel benchmark.
European customers have not accepted index-linking.

title: Singapore: 5% surcharge copied from France, no local pilot
statement: Apply a 5% freight surcharge in Singapore on 1 November 2024, copying the France approach without a local pilot.
expected_outcome: +$1.8M a quarter with churn loss of 1.0% of baseline.

evidence.excerpt: A 5% freight surcharge was applied in Singapore on 1 November 2024, copying the France approach without a local pilot.

title: Germany: hold fixed pricing for the top 20 strategic accounts
statement: Hold fixed pricing for the twenty largest German strategic accounts through 2026, regardless of any surcharge programme.
rationale: A regional competitor is expected to cut contract rates in early 2026 to win strategic accounts.

evidence.excerpt: Hold fixed pricing for the twenty largest German strategic accounts through 2026, regardless of any surcharge programme.

title: France: extend 5% to mid-market shippers as a two-region pilot
statement: Extend the 5% surcharge to French mid-market shippers as a two-region pilot only, starting January 2026, and stop if churn loss passes 1.2%.
rationale: Mid-market churn loss at 5% is estimated between 0.9% and 1.4% of baseline, so the upper end would breach the guardrail.
alternatives: Extend to all French mid-market shippers at once

evidence.excerpt: Proposal to extend the 5% freight surcharge to French mid-market shippers who were outside the 2024 scope.
Extend the 5% surcharge to French mid-market shippers as a two-region pilot only, starting January 2026, and stop if churn loss passes 1.2%.
